en: The Single Scroll of the True Suchness Dharma of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Great Compassionate Wisdom Seal,
Pervading the Dharmadhātu to Benefit Sentient Beings.
Translated during the Great Tang Dynasty by the Special Advance, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, with the Rank of Kai-fu Yi-tong.

The Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra—posthumously titled Duke of Sugu by the Three Departments, granted the rank of Minister of Works, and conferred the posthumous name Dapianzheng (Great Discriminating and Upright), as well as Da Guangzhi (Greatly Vast Wisdom)—translates this at my request by the sacred command of Vairocana.
He then taught the mudrā and dharma of the Mother of Wisdom, Mahāprajñāpāramitā Avalokiteśvarī.
If there is a practitioner of yoga who wishes to be born in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss to benefit sentient beings, [he should practice as follows].
Then, from an ācārya who possesses mature wisdom,
he received the ritual procedures for the Lotus-Vajra (Padmavajra) and performed the dharma of recitation while extensively presenting offerings.
Within that mandala, place an incense burner.
This incense burner embodies the appearance of Avalokiteśvara pervading the entire dharmadhātu.
What constitutes this appearance?
Regarding that fragrance seal, one should form the syllable *hrīḥ*.
It is the principle that the activity of wisdom is ungraspable;
it subsumes the fourfold meaning, with the syllables *hūṃ*, *vaṃ*, *aḥ*, and *hoḥ* combined into a single character.
Its Sanskrit equivalent is this: *He*.
The syllable *He* signifies that the cause of all phenomena is unattainable;
the syllable *Ra* signifies purity and freedom from defilement.
The character "I" (伊) is sovereign and ungraspable;
the character "E" (惡) is fundamentally neither born nor extinguished.
This is the meaning of accordance with reality.
Fundamentally unborn and unceasing,
sovereign and ungraspable,
pure and free from defilement.
The causes of all phenomena are unobtainable;
this is the meaning of "reversal.
The correspondence between reversal and conformity reveals the text of the Incense Seal.
I have drawn this diagram.
This wondrous seal is named "Great Compassion that Extracts Suffering. Why is this so?
By means of the sequence of burning,
the true principle is revealed;
when it is completely burned away, [the truth is manifest].
Whether the visualization proceeds in forward or reverse order, it ultimately returns to the dharma of emptiness;
one should observe this state.
It originates from the single syllable *hrīḥ*.
From the syllables Oṃ Vajradharma and so forth— five syllables in total—
there arise immeasurable gates of letters (*akṣaramukha*) within each individual syllable.
From each gate of letters, there are manifested the bodies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Each and every transformation body pervades the Dharma-realm to benefit sentient beings;
therefore, the practitioner attains immeasurable merit,
fulfills *siddhi*, and receives the empowerment of all Buddhas.
Therefore, the practitioner attains stability and peace in the present life, free from all obstacles;
like a wondrous lotus,
they are cherished by all who behold them.
Having been reborn, they attain birth within a superior lotus in the Land of Ultimate Bliss;
those with sharp faculties, wisdom, and skillful means behold the Buddha in their present bodies.
They attain a dhāraṇī named "Untainted by the World.
In whatever place they are born, their bodies emit a wondrous fragrance.
Pervading the lands of the ten directions,
sentient beings are perfumed by it,
and all realize non-retrogression.
Such merits as these cannot be fully described.
Upon the cover of the incense burner,
one may carve the syllable *vajradharma*.
Add the syllable *Oṃ* at the beginning to form a five-syllable mantra; one should rotate it clockwise around the center of the canopy.
At its center, one should establish the *samaya*-form, which is a single-pronged vajra surmounted by an eight-petaled lotus flower.
The five characters mentioned above encircle this samaya;
"samaya" is the form of one's original vow.
If one beholds this form, pays homage, and maintains focused mindfulness, [one shall attain realization].
One immediately realizes the nature of the lotus;
thus, those born in Sukhāvatī are no longer defiled by the world.
Even if they should interact with the mundane world, [they remain unstained].
Delivering sentient beings like a lotus flower, untainted by any defilements—
this realization of the realm of fruition is entirely due to the power of original vows made in the past.
Therefore, the practitioner should establish this samaya-form and,
with single-minded mindfulness, form this mental image:
that the fragrant smoke of the syllable *HŪṂ* constitutes this samaya-form.
This form further becomes the physical body of the Honored One (bimba),
signifying that the original vow made during the causal stage has thus become the form and color of the resultant stage.
This is the meaning of the samaya.
At the time of burning incense, one should form the mudrā of the principal deity and recite this root mantra while sealing it with the mudrā.
One will immediately achieve accomplishment.
The diagram of the parasol is as follows.
The diagram is described briefly above in the section on the incense mudrā.
One shall attain entry into this wheel and reach unsurpassed bodhi.
If one desires to recite the mantra constantly without interruption,
yet has not abandoned discursive attachment and is inclined toward indolence, [one will fail].
Relying solely upon this sublime seal,
one should burn incense such as sandalwood and lotus;
thus, one who performs the rite of burning incense every day.
One then accomplishes the constant practice of reciting and upholding the Vajra-dharmaprabha.
Why is this? Because it is as explained above regarding the meaning of the syllables of the mantra.
Because all [deities] can be manifested through this incense mudrā,
it is the root mudrā:
the two hands form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*).
Join the tips of the two index fingers like lotus petals;
the two thumbs should be placed side by side.
The mantra is as follows:
If a person upholds this single-syllable mantra,
they will be able to eliminate all calamities and diseases;
after the end of their life, they shall attain rebirth in the supreme grade of Sukhāvatī.
All other great worldly and supramundane aspirations that one seeks will be sustained and accomplished;
how much more so for those who practice according to these teachings—
every *siddhi* will be perfected before long.
The *Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Incense-True-Suchness Seal Dharma* is hereby completed.
One fascicle of the *Avalokiteśvara Sublime Incense Seal Dharma*. Written on the first day of the middle month of summer in the year of the Dragon (1735) of the Hyōhō era.
Using the annotated manuscript of Master Jingyan as the basis for collation,
I have had it carved into printing blocks;
may the radiance of the incense smoke illuminate True Suchness, its clouds covering the atoms of all lands.
Recorded by the śramaṇa Mudo of Rinsha at Myōon-in in Hasedera, Yamato.
